messages.subject: Coloring specific points
parts:
So I'm creating a map using ggplot of the lower 48 zipcodes for the US.

I've got the map looking exactly the way I'd like it to look, but I'm not having any luck doing some additional plot aspects.

Basically I'd like all the points to be the 'darkkhaki' color and I'd like the points for the zipcodes that start with a 0 to be white.  (I've also got to create a similar visualization where the zipcodes that start with a 49 are white)

I haven't been able to manipulate any of the solutions on here or elsewhere to solve my problem.

I've attached the work I've got so far

zipcode <- read.csv(file="W13 zipcodes.txt", sep=",", head=F)
zipcode

#load ggplot2 package
require(ggplot2)
library(ggplot2)

#Data Mining
zipcode$V4 = substr(zipcode$V2, 1, 1) #sets the value in V4 to the first value of V2
zipcode$V5 = -abs(zipcode$V5)  #Sets the V5 column negative




bf = ggplot(data=zipcode) + geom_point(aes(x=zipcode$V5, y=zipcode$V6), colour = 'darkkhaki', shape = ".")
bf = bf + theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill='dimgray'), panel.grid = element_blank())

# simplify display and limit to the "lower 48"
bf = bf + scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-125, -66)) 
bf = bf + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(25, 50))

# don't need axis labels
bf = bf + labs(x=NULL, y=NULL)
bf

Thanks!
mary ellen

messages.subject: Re: Coloring specific points
parts:
Wanted to reply to myself since I solved my problem already.

Here is what I did if it helps anyone else or anyone has any alternatives.

Created myself a variable for the colour part of the plot aesthetic

colour = ifelse(zipcode$V2 <= 10000, "white", "darkkhaki")

#Graph with zipcodes starting with 0
bf0 = ggplot(data=zipcode) + geom_point(aes(x=zipcode$V5, y=zipcode$V6), colour = colour, shape = ".")
bf0 = bf0 + theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill='dimgray'), panel.grid = element_blank())
# simplify display and limit to the "lower 48"

bf0 = bf0 + scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-125, -66)) 
bf0 = bf0 + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(25, 50))

bf0 = bf0 + labs(x=NULL, y=NULL)
bf0


For the selection of just the zip codes that started with 49 I created a new variable 
micolour = ifelse(zipcode$V2 < 49000, "darkkhaki", ifelse(zipcode$V2 > 50000, "darkkhaki", "white"))
